9ce6d6a2-dbc5-444a-bc5d-3e56deba389e.topic: Explanation of how rotational motion works, covering angular velocity, torque, and moment of inertia.
9ce6d6a2-dbc5-444a-bc5d-3e56deba389e.subtitles:
```webvtt
WEBVTT

00:00.000 --> 00:04.000
Welcome to this lesson on rotational motion.

00:04.000 --> 00:06.000
Let's explore angular velocity,

00:06.000 --> 00:08.500
torque, and moment of inertia.

00:08.500 --> 00:12.000
Angular velocity is the rate of change
of angular displacement.

00:12.000 --> 00:15.500
Torque is a rotational force causing
angular acceleration.

00:15.500 --> 00:20.000
Moment of inertia is the resistance
to change in rotational motion.

00:20.000 --> 00:26.000
The relationship between these is Torque
equals moment of inertia times angular acceleration.

00:26.000 --> 00:30.000
Let's summarize the key points.

00:30.000 --> 00:34.000
First, angular velocity describes how
fast something rotates.

00:34.000 --> 00:37.000
Second, torque is a twisting force.

00:37.000 --> 00:40.000
And third, moment of inertia is the
resistance to twisting.

00:40.000 --> 00:41.700
Now you understand rotational motion!

00:41.700 --> 00:44.000

```
